newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Popocatepetl volcano throws up gas, rocks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Popocatepetl volcano throws up gas, rocks.

text.p: Mexico's famous Popocatepetl volcano sent up huge plumes of black smoke and gases and spewed out red-hot rocks late on Sunday in its most violent spurt of activity in the last two years.

"They were the biggest movements recorded in the last two years," Guillermo Malgarejo, the head of the Civil Protection Force in the state of Puebla where the snow-capped volcano lies 50 miles (80 km) east of the capital, said on Monday.

TV footage showed "Popo" ominously half-shrouded in blackened clouds on Monday. Three small earthquakes triggered a chain reaction of activity and sent panic waves through the local population living in the foothills, experts said.
The three quakes, all between 2.0 and 3.0 on the open-ended Richter scale, sufficiently stirred up Popocatepetl's rock strata to force blocked volcanic ducts to blow, Malgarejo said.
"We received a wave of phone calls asking what to do," Malgarejo said. "The situation is very worrying for local people," he said.

Volcanologist Alejandro Rivera Dominguez told state-owned news agency Notimex that the first quake at 1938 (0138 GMT on Monday) provoked a hail of red-hot ash to spew out of the volcano with further minor eruptions for the next two hours.
Edgy locals were frightened by the red ash reflecting in the crisp, white snow, Rivera added.
Experts moved onto the volcano's flanks on Monday morning in a bid to evaluate exactly what happened, especially inside the volcano's huge crater, Rivera said.
Persistent activity at Popocatepetl, which in Nahuatl means "Smoking Mountain", has forced Puebla authorities to put in a place an emergency evacuation plan.
Soldiers are permanently stationed in the foothills and constantly patrol the agricultural lands, ready to move out the estimated 300,000 people who live there in case of a full-scale eruption.

For months, Puebla state authorities have declared a "yellow alert" or "on guard" warning because of the threat from Popocatepetl. The next stage up is a red alert when an immediate evacuation would be ordered.
